findings.issue_text: [BUG] LoginValues/formSchema is not extended for backupCode, so the zodResolver strips the field and next-auth authorize never receives it. The credentials provider's new `credentials.backupCode` branch (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts) is unreachable from the login page: zodResolver only passes schema-declared fields to signIn, so a user who lost their authenticator and submits a backup code gets SecondFactorRequired/incorrect-2fa instead of logging in — the entire lost-access login path is dead on arrival unless formSchema (outside the diff) is also updated.

[BUG] The disable handler reads user.backupCodes but the diff does not show backupCodes being added to the earlier prisma user select in this file. If the pre-existing user fetch uses an explicit select (typical for this endpoint, which already selects twoFactorSecret/twoFactorEnabled), user.backupCodes is undefined and every lost-access disable attempt returns MissingBackupCodes even when codes exist.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code consumption in the disable path never marks the used code, and the comment acknowledges this, but there is no compensating write anywhere in the disable flow. A single backup code can disable 2FA repeatedly (and, per the delete-all-at-end write, that is moot here) — but the login-path deletion model (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts) and the disable-path model diverge: one burns a single code, the other relies on nuking all codes at disable time, so any future reuse of this snippet copies the wrong invariant.

[ADVISORY] formatBackupCode is referenced inside handleSetup (defined above it) via a const arrow function declared later in the component body. Works only because handleSetup runs after render; if anyone hoists handleSetup into a useCallback before the const declaration (the file already uses useCallbackRef for handleEnable), the next refactor hits a TDZ ReferenceError — change-safety smell, not a current failure.

[ADVISORY] backupCodes state is typed useState([]) so formatBackupCode(code: string) receives an implicit any[] element and body.backupCodes is unvalidated server JSON. TypeScript infers never[]/any[]; a malformed setup response (or a non-array backupCodes) makes body.backupCodes.map throw inside handleSetup, leaving the modal stuck on ConfirmPassword with no error message shown to the user.

[BUG] The login zod formSchema is never updated to include backupCode, so zodResolver strips the backupCode field before it reaches signIn, making the entire backup-code login path unreachable. The diff adds backupCode to LoginValues (line 43), to the Credentials provider (next-auth-options.ts line 65), and renders BackupCode input, but the resolver `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` (line 67) is unchanged and the diff never touches formSchema. zod strips unknown keys by default, so handleSubmit delivers credentials without backupCode; next-auth's authorize falls into the totp branch and returns SecondFactorRequired. A user who clicks 'Lost access' and enters a valid backup code always gets '2fa required' — the feature silently does not work on the login page.

[BUG] JSON.parse of the decrypted backupCodes blob is unguarded, so a corrupt or legacy-format stored value crashes the disable endpoint with an unhandled exception and a 500 instead of a 4xx. A user whose user.backupCodes column contains anything that is not a JSON array of strings (e.g. data written by a prior schema shape, or truncation) hits an uncaught SyntaxError inside the handler when attempting to disable 2FA with a backup code — the one flow designed for users who cannot use TOTP — and gets a 500 with no error message in the modal.

[BUG] Client-side minLength=10 counts the dash, so a dashed 10-character input ('XXXXX-XXXX') passes HTML validation while the server strips the dash and rejects the 9-character code. A user who types a 9-hex-character code with a dash satisfies the required/minLength constraints, the form submits, and the server's backupCodes.indexOf() lookup fails, returning IncorrectBackupCode for a code-length the UI itself invited via the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder — confusing dead-end with no client-side hint that 10 or 11 chars including dash are required.

[ADVISORY] Backup codes are displayed exactly once inside the modal, and any dismissal other than the explicit Close button (Escape key, overlay click, onOpenChange) loses them permanently with no re-view or regenerate feature anywhere in the diff. The dialog's onOpenChange still closes on Escape/overlay click while step === DisplayBackupCodes; resetState is only wired to the Close button. A user who dismisses the dialog before downloading/copying can never retrieve the codes again — the diff adds no 'view backup codes' or 'regenerate' settings path, so 'missing_backup_codes' error messaging ('generate them in your settings') points at a capability that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] Every call to setup silently overwrites user.backupCodes with a fresh set, invalidating previously issued codes without user confirmation or any consumer that regenerates codes independently of full 2FA re-setup. Re-running the setup flow (e.g. a user re-enabling or reconfiguring 2FA) destroys outstanding backup codes that may be printed in a drawer; previously distributed codes stop working with no warning. There is also no standalone 'regenerate backup codes' endpoint in the diff, so the MissingBackupCodes recovery path advertised in the UI requires a full disable/re-enable cycle.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code consumption is a read-then-write with no atomicity, so two concurrent login attempts with the same code both succeed. indexOf + prisma.update is not atomic; two parallel requests presenting the same valid code both read the un-consumed array and both authenticate, defeating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee stated in the user-facing copy (backup_code_instructions).

[BUG] The only test coverage in the diff exercises the enable-flow display/copy/download of backup codes; the backup-code login path and the backup-code disable path have zero tests, a gap the diff itself acknowledges. The diff's own TODO at line 12 ('TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup') concedes that the two highest-risk new behaviors — authenticating via next-auth authorize with a consumed-code write (next-auth-options.ts lines 128-156) and the disable.ts backup branch — ship with no verification. A regression in either (e.g. the F1 resolver stripping above, or the null-rewrite producing '[null,null,...]' blobs) would pass the existing e2e suite unnoticed.

[BUG] The diff ships a test assertion the diff itself annotates as broken ('FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked'), so the two-factor-enabled assertion in the login.2fa e2e suite verifies nothing. The guard test for 2FA enabling passes even when the switch is off, so regressions in the enable flow silently pass CI; the FIXME was added in this diff rather than fixed, meaning knowingly-broken coverage is being committed.

[ADVISORY] The single-use invariant of backup codes (the core security property of the feature) has no test anywhere in this diff — the e2e TODO at apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts line 12 explicitly defers 'login + disabling 2fa with backup' tests. A regression that fails to null-out a consumed code (e.g. someone later 'simplifies' the update call or moves it behind a conditional) would turn single-use codes into reusable credentials and no test would catch it; the most security-sensitive behavior in the diff is exactly the untested one.

[ADVISORY] The 'missing_backup_codes' message instructs users to 'generate them in your settings', but this diff adds no regenerate/backup-codes-management UI or API anywhere — the only path that mints codes is the full disable-and-re-enable 2FA flow. A user with 2FA enabled but no backup codes (e.g. codes created before this migration, or codes exhausted at login via next-auth-options.ts consumption) follows the message into settings and finds no generator, producing a dead-end support incident; the error text promises a feature the diff does not ship.

[ADVISORY] Exhausted-code users get the wrong error: the array is persisted with null placeholders after consumption, so once all 10 codes are burned, indexOf returns -1 and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user who legitimately used all their codes keeps retrying 'incorrect' codes with no signal that none remain, when the codebase already has a MissingBackupCodes error designed for exactly this state (unused at this site).

[ADVISORY] The tabIndex={-1} change on the shared PasswordField eye-toggle button in packages/ui is not traceable to the backup-codes requirement — it is a global keyboard-navigation behavior change to a design-system component riding along in the feature diff. Every PasswordField in the product (password login, disable-2FA, org settings, etc.) loses the eye toggle from tab order in one release, affecting keyboard users app-wide with no requirement covering it; if intentional it belongs in its own a11y change with its own review/testing, and it is not covered by any test in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Setup regenerates and persists encrypted backup codes on every /setup call, and the download URL blob is only cleaned up via the revoke on a subsequent setup call, never when the dialog is closed or the component unmounts. Each abandoned/restarted setup cycle overwrites the stored codes (previous printed/downloaded copies become stale without the user being warned that old codes are invalidated), and each dialog session leaks one object URL per enable attempt until the next setup call.

[BUG] Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-encrypt write (JSON.parse of the whole list, indexOf, then prisma.user.update with the re-encrypted whole list) with no transaction, no row lock, and no per-code tombstone, so two concurrent logins using the same (or different) backup codes both read the same plaintext list and the second update silently resurrects the code the first login consumed. A single backup code can be replayed: two parallel login attempts with the same code both pass verification and each writes back its own copy of the array with only its own index nulled, re-adding the other's consumed code; the same lost-update also lets a consumed code survive when two different codes are used concurrently. This defeats the 'each code can be used exactly once' invariant the UI copy promises.

[BUG] LoginValues gains a backupCode field but the zodResolver schema (formSchema) is not updated in this diff, and zodResolver strips keys the schema does not declare, so backupCode is dropped from the submitted credentials and the credentials-backupCode branch in next-auth-options.ts is never reached from the login page. A user who clicks 'Lost access' on the login page and enters a valid backup code gets the SecondFactorRequired/incorrect-TOTP error path instead of logging in — the entire lost-access recovery flow is dead on arrival at login time, while the disable-2FA modal path (which posts the field explicitly via TwoFactorAuthAPI) works.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification block (encryption-key guard, MissingBackupCodes check, decrypt, dash-stripped indexOf) is a near-verbatim copy of the same block in next-auth-options.ts, and the two copies already differ in behavior: the login copy consumes the matched code, the disable copy deliberately does not. The next change to backup-code verification (e.g. case-insensitive matching, rate limiting, consuming on disable) must be made in two places or the auth path and the disable path silently diverge — the same drift pattern the duplicated client/server error handling in this PR already exhibits.

[ADVISORY] The missing_backup_codes message instructs users to 'generate them in your settings', but the only code path in this diff that (re)generates backup codes is the setup endpoint, which is invoked exclusively from the enable-2FA wizard and overwrites the user's TOTP secret; no settings UI can regenerate codes for a user who already has 2FA enabled. Every user who had 2FA enabled before this migration (backupCodes=null) or who re-ran setup without completing it sees a message pointing at a flow that does not exist; they cannot obtain backup codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA entirely.

[ADVISORY] At the DisplayBackupCodes step the codes are shown exactly once with no guard against dismissal: the Dialog's onOpenChange (click outside / Escape) closes the modal and the codes state is lost with the unmount, with no confirmation and no later retrieval path. A user who dismisses the dialog at that step without clicking download/copy permanently loses all ten backup codes and has no way to regenerate them short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code comparison uses case-sensitive indexOf against lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes().toString('hex')), while the input field applies no normalization — an input entered with uppercase characters (common on mobile with auto-capitalize) is rejected as incorrect. Legitimate users typing or auto-correcting the code into uppercase get 'Backup code is incorrect' with no indication that case matters; the same latent mismatch exists in the login path's indexOf.

[ADVISORY] The new BackupCode component's exported function is internally named TwoFactor (copy-paste from TwoFactor.tsx), creating a confusable pair with the adjacent TwoFactor component that renders a completely different input. The next editor touching auth components sees `TwoFactor` imported from BackupCode.tsx (as in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx) and can reasonably assume it renders the TOTP digit inputs; any refactor that routes to 'TwoFactor' picks the wrong form.

[ADVISORY] The setup endpoint persists freshly generated backupCodes (and resets twoFactorSecret) on every setup call, before the user has confirmed the TOTP code — repeated setup invocations silently invalidate any backup codes the user previously saved. A user who saved codes, then re-opens the enable wizard (or any client that re-POSTs setup), has the stored codes replaced; the previously printed/downloaded codes stop working with only the wizard as witness, and nothing in the response or UI communicates the invalidation of old codes.

[BUG] The enable flow silently changed from 'onEnable() immediately on success' to 'onEnable() only via the backup-codes Close button', so dismissing the dialog by any other path (X button, Escape, backdrop click via onOpenChange) while on SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes leaves the parent state stale even though the server has already enabled 2FA. The user completes 2FA setup server-side (twoFactorEnabled was set true by the enable endpoint), then closes the dialog with Escape/backdrop; onEnable never fires, the settings UI still shows 2FA as disabled, and the user may re-run setup — regenerating secrets and invalidating their just-saved authenticator binding. The original accepted objective (parent notified exactly on successful enable) was rewritten in review without a compensating handler on onOpenChange.

[BUG] Every call to the setup endpoint regenerates and overwrites all stored backup codes, silently invalidating backup codes the user previously downloaded/copied, with no explicit user acceptance of that revocation. A user who saved their backup codes, then reopens the 2FA setup dialog just to re-view the QR code (a plausible flow, since setup runs before 2FA is confirmed enabled), gets 10 brand-new codes; the old printed/saved codes fail at login with 'Backup code is incorrect' and the user is locked out of the lost-access path they may have relied on. The one-time-use intent ('Each backup code can be used exactly once') is silently upgraded to 'codes can also be mass-revoked as a side effect of re-setup' without that being part of the accepted feature scope.

[ADVISORY] The backup-codes Blob URL is created and displayed but onOpenChange-driven dismissal of the dialog during DisplayBackupCodes neither revokes the object URL nor resets step/backupCodes state, so reopening the dialog later can render stale codes from a previous setup run. After setup regenerates codes server-side, a user reopening the enable dialog before re-running setup sees the previous session's codes (the WithStep for DisplayBackupCodes persists because resetState only runs via cancel/close buttons, which are hidden on that step); they copy/download codes that are already invalid on the server. Also leaks an unrevoked Blob URL per re-render path since revokeObjectURL only happens on the next setup call.

[BUG] Backup code consumption uses a non-atomic read-decrypt-match-write, so two concurrent login requests with the same code both pass the indexOf check before either update lands, letting a single-use backup code be replayed. An attacker who observes/intercepts one backup-code login (or a user with two parallel tabs) can immediately reuse the same code for a second authenticated login, defeating the single-use guarantee the UI text promises ('Each backup code can be used exactly once'). Needs an atomic conditional update or a used-codes set with a unique constraint.

[BUG] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) runs without try/catch, so a corrupt or wrongly-encrypted backupCodes value throws inside NextAuth's authorize and surfaces as an opaque 500/internal error instead of a handled auth error. A user whose backupCodes column was written by a deploy with a different CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or any corrupted row) gets InternalServerError on every login attempt instead of a recoverable message, and the same unhandled throw exists in the disable endpoint at apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:53.

[ADVISORY] The disable endpoint accepts the backup code without any rate limiting on the code-guessing path, unlike the TOTP path's environment, and codes are matched with a non-constant-time indexOf. An attacker who has already obtained the account password (e.g. via a leak) can brute-force the 40-bit code space at network speed to disable 2FA; 10 codes of 5 random bytes give only ~2^36 effective guesses per account. Even the login path should be confirmed to rate-limit the backupCode branch specifically.

[ADVISORY] Backup code comparison is case-sensitive against lowercase hex storage while the input field has no normalization, so uppercase input is rejected as an incorrect code. Legitimate users typing codes copied with uppercase formatting (common from password managers or manual transcription) get 'Backup code is incorrect' and burn retry attempts; one .toLowerCase() on the normalized input removes the mismatch.

[ADVISORY] Hitting the setup endpoint regenerates and overwrites backupCodes before the user has confirmed TOTP enrollment, silently invalidating any previously displayed backup codes. A user who opens the 2FA setup dialog twice (or abandons it after viewing codes) invalidates codes they already saved to their password manager, discovering this only when locked out and trying 'lost access'. Codes should only rotate on successful enable, mirroring how the secret is handled.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code flow has zero functional coverage for its security-critical path — the TODO comments in this same diff acknowledge login and disable-with-backup-code are untested, and nothing exercises single-use consumption. A regression that makes backup codes reusable, or that fails to consume them on login, would ship undetected; the e2e test only covers the cosmetic download/copy/close buttons during enrollment.

[BUG] The enable-2fa assertion `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` awaits a Promise<boolean> and asserts truthiness of the promise object, so it passes unconditionally whether or not the switch is checked. The e2e test reports 2FA enabling as verified even when the toggle fails to enable; a regression that breaks the switch (the diff's own FIXME comment confirms it 'passes even when switch is not checked') ships green, giving false confidence that the core 2FA enable path works. The correct assertion is `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-codes e2e block only asserts the download filename and that a toast appeared, leaving the file content and clipboard content explicitly unchecked ('TODO: check file content', 'TODO: check clipboard content'). A regression that renders empty/garbled backup codes, or a copy button that copies the wrong text, still passes this test — the user would save or copy codes they can never log in with, and CI would not catch it. At minimum the download path can assert real content (download.path()/failure text) rather than only the suggested filename.

[ADVISORY] The two new server-side backup-code paths added in this diff — login authorization with a consumed backup code (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts backup branch) and 2FA disable via backup code (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts) — have no test coverage; the diff's own TODO comment admits 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. The single-use burn logic (backupCodes[index] = null followed by re-encrypt) and the disable-with-backup-code branch are security-critical state transitions that nothing in this diff or the suite exercises; a regression there (e.g. codes not consumed, allowing code reuse) would reach production undetected.

[ADVISORY] The setup endpoint unconditionally overwrites user.backupCodes with freshly generated codes on every call, destroying the previously stored (possibly still unused) backup codes before the user has confirmed any completion step. A user who already has valid, unburned backup codes and merely re-opens the 2FA setup flow (then abandons it without finishing enable) silently loses their only recovery codes — the old encrypted values are overwritten at setup time and the displayed replacement codes are never persisted-visible unless the flow is completed; no confirmation or regeneration gate exists.

[BUG] Closing the dialog via Escape/outside-click (Dialog onOpenChange) while on the DisplayBackupCodes step bypasses both resetState() and onEnable(), so 2FA is enabled server-side but the parent is never notified and the modal reopens stuck on the backup-codes step. User completes TOTP entry, presses Escape instead of the Close button: the modal closes without onEnable(), the surrounding settings page still shows 2FA as disabled, and reopening the dialog shows stale backup codes with no Cancel button (Cancel is hidden at that step), forcing a refresh; the enabled-but-unreported state is a silent partial success on the user-facing enable flow.

[BUG] The copy button shows the 'backup_codes_copied' success toast unconditionally, without awaiting or catching the promise returned by navigator.clipboard.writeText. When clipboard write fails (document not focused, permission denied, non-secure context), the promise rejects unhandled and the user sees 'Backup codes copied!' while nothing was copied — the only copy path for one-time recovery codes reports success while doing nothing, and the user may close the dialog believing the codes are saved.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code consumption is a check-then-act read-then-write (JSON.parse of the stored list, indexOf, then a full-list update) with no atomic claim, so two concurrent logins presenting the same code both pass indexOf and both consume it. The 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee (stated verbatim in backup_code_instructions) is broken under concurrency: two simultaneous sign-in requests with the same code both succeed, and a parallel login request can also resurrect an already-null'ed slot by racing the rewrite — the code effectively becomes reusable.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code matching compares case-sensitively against lowercase hex codes (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')) after only stripping dashes, with no case normalization of user input. A user who types their backup code in uppercase (the placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX' invites that reading, and there is no autocapitalize=false on the input) always gets 'Backup code is incorrect.' on both login and disable paths despite entering the right characters — a confusing, unrecoverable-feeling failure for users in exactly the lost-access scenario the feature exists for.

[ADVISORY] The blob object URL created in handleSetup is only revoked when a subsequent setup call runs; it is never revoked on dialog close, cancel, or unmount. Each completed setup run leaks a Blob (containing live recovery codes) in the page's blob store for the lifetime of the session; repeated setup attempts accumulate them, and sensitive backup-code content lingers in memory/blob storage longer than the UI implies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Backup code consumption uses a non-atomic read-decrypt-match-write, so two concurrent login requests with the same code both pass the indexOf check before either update lands, letting a single-use backup code be replayed. An attacker who observes/intercepts one backup-code login (or a user with two parallel tabs) can immediately reuse the same code for a second authenticated login, defeating the single-use guarantee the UI text promises ('Each backup code can be used exactly once'). Needs an atomic conditional update or a used-codes set with a unique constraint.
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race condition: backup codes are read/decrypted and checked in memory, then written back non-atomically, allowing two concurrent requests with the same backup code to both pass the check and consume it twice, breaking one-time-use semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) runs without try/catch, so a corrupt or wrongly-encrypted backupCodes value throws inside NextAuth's authorize and surfaces as an opaque 500/internal error instead of a handled auth error. A user whose backupCodes column was written by a deploy with a different CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or any corrupted row) gets InternalServerError on every login attempt instead of a recoverable message, and the same unhandled throw exists in the disable endpoint at apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:53.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the new backup-code login path does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` without any try/catch. If `user.backupCodes` is corrupt or decrypt fails (e.g., wrong `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` used when it was written), `symmetricDecrypt` or `JSON.parse` can throw, producing an unhandled exception rather than a controlled auth error. The same unguarded `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` exists in the new disable flow in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (the added backup-code branch), which would likewise throw and result in a 500 response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The disable endpoint accepts the backup code without any rate limiting on the code-guessing path, unlike the TOTP path's environment, and codes are matched with a non-constant-time indexOf. An attacker who has already obtained the account password (e.g. via a leak) can brute-force the 40-bit code space at network speed to disable 2FA; 10 codes of 5 random bytes give only ~2^36 effective guesses per account. Even the login path should be confirmed to rate-limit the backupCode branch specifically.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new backup-code authentication path to the 2FA disable API (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`: `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) { ... const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...) }`) with no visible rate limiting/throttling in that handler. Backup codes are generated as 10 hex chars (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`), so they are static 40-bit secrets; without endpoint throttling, an attacker who already knows the password can repeatedly POST guesses to `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable` until a match, and the match check is a straightforward `indexOf` (not constant-time). The finding’s comparison to “unlike the TOTP path” may be overstated, but the lack of rate limiting on the newly introduced backup-code disable path is directly supported by the diff and is a security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backup code comparison is case-sensitive against lowercase hex storage while the input field has no normalization, so uppercase input is rejected as an incorrect code. Legitimate users typing codes copied with uppercase formatting (common from password managers or manual transcription) get 'Backup code is incorrect' and burn retry attempts; one .toLowerCase() on the normalized input removes the mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex via `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts), but both verification paths compare the stored codes against the raw user input with only dash removal: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in the disable API (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts) and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in NextAuth authorize (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts). Since there is no `.toLowerCase()` (or other normalization) on the input, uppercase user-entered backup codes will not match and will be rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The setup endpoint unconditionally overwrites user.backupCodes with freshly generated codes on every call, destroying the previously stored (possibly still unused) backup codes before the user has confirmed any completion step. A user who already has valid, unburned backup codes and merely re-opens the 2FA setup flow (then abandons it without finishing enable) silently loses their only recovery codes — the old encrypted values are overwritten at setup time and the displayed replacement codes are never persisted-visible unless the flow is completed; no confirmation or regeneration gate exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup handler now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ... } })` on every successful setup call. This overwrites any previously stored (encrypted) backup codes before the user completes the enable flow. The UI change in `EnableTwoFactorModal` only shows the backup codes after `handleEnable` succeeds (it switches to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` only after the enable endpoint returns 200), so a user can trigger setup (thus replacing stored codes) and then abandon before ever being shown the new codes, effectively losing recovery codes. The diff shows no regeneration/confirmation gate around persisting backup codes at setup time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Closing the dialog via Escape/outside-click (Dialog onOpenChange) while on the DisplayBackupCodes step bypasses both resetState() and onEnable(), so 2FA is enabled server-side but the parent is never notified and the modal reopens stuck on the backup-codes step. User completes TOTP entry, presses Escape instead of the Close button: the modal closes without onEnable(), the surrounding settings page still shows 2FA as disabled, and reopening the dialog shows stale backup codes with no Cancel button (Cancel is hidden at that step), forcing a refresh; the enabled-but-unreported state is a silent partial success on the user-facing enable flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, after successful TOTP verification `handleEnable` no longer calls `onEnable()`; it only does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and returns (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, around the `if (response.status === 200)` in `handleEnable`). The only place that calls both `resetState()` and `onEnable()` is the explicit “close” button in the `DisplayBackupCodes` step (`backup-codes-close`). However the `Dialog` is wired as `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` with no wrapper to invoke `resetState()`/`onEnable()` when the dialog is closed via Escape or outside-click. Therefore closing the modal during `DisplayBackupCodes` can leave 2FA enabled server-side but the parent never notified, and the internal `step` state can remain `DisplayBackupCodes` when reopened (also causing the Cancel button to remain hidden at that step).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The copy button shows the 'backup_codes_copied' success toast unconditionally, without awaiting or catching the promise returned by navigator.clipboard.writeText. When clipboard write fails (document not focused, permission denied, non-secure context), the promise rejects unhandled and the user sees 'Backup codes copied!' while nothing was copied — the only copy path for one-time recovery codes reports success while doing nothing, and the user may close the dialog believing the codes are saved.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, the copy button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` but does not `await` it or attach `.then/.catch` before calling `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`. This means the success toast is displayed even if the clipboard write fails, and a rejection would be unhandled. This behavior is directly visible in the diff in the `data-testid="backup-codes-copy"` onClick block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backup-code consumption is a check-then-act read-then-write (JSON.parse of the stored list, indexOf, then a full-list update) with no atomic claim, so two concurrent logins presenting the same code both pass indexOf and both consume it. The 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee (stated verbatim in backup_code_instructions) is broken under concurrency: two simultaneous sign-in requests with the same code both succeed, and a parallel login request can also resurrect an already-null'ed slot by racing the rewrite — the code effectively becomes reusable.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code “consumption” is implemented as: decrypt full `user.backupCodes` JSON array → `indexOf()` match → mutate in-memory (`backupCodes[index] = null`) → `prisma.user.update({ backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) })`. There is no atomic/conditional update or transaction tying the read to the write, so concurrent authorize calls can both validate the same code before either update lands (both sign-ins succeed). Additionally, concurrent uses of *different* backup codes can lose one of the nullifications due to last-write-wins on the full-list rewrite, effectively making a code reusable. This breaks the stated “used exactly once” guarantee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backup-code matching compares case-sensitively against lowercase hex codes (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')) after only stripping dashes, with no case normalization of user input. A user who types their backup code in uppercase (the placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX' invites that reading, and there is no autocapitalize=false on the input) always gets 'Backup code is incorrect.' on both login and disable paths despite entering the right characters — a confusing, unrecoverable-feeling failure for users in exactly the lost-access scenario the feature exists for.

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`). On both verification paths, the code only strips dashes and then does a case-sensitive `indexOf` match (`credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) with no `.toLowerCase()` normalization. Therefore, if a user enters the correct characters but in uppercase (plausible given placeholder `"XXXXX-XXXXX"` in `BackupCode.tsx` and no input autocapitalize control shown), the match fails and returns `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The blob object URL created in handleSetup is only revoked when a subsequent setup call runs; it is never revoked on dialog close, cancel, or unmount. Each completed setup run leaks a Blob (containing live recovery codes) in the page's blob store for the lifetime of the session; repeated setup attempts accumulate them, and sensitive backup-code content lingers in memory/blob storage longer than the UI implies.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.handleSetup`, a Blob URL is created and stored in state (`setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))`). The code only revokes the *previous* URL when another setup call happens (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`). On cancel/close/reset/unmount there is no revocation: `resetState()` clears password/error/step but does not clear or revoke `backupCodesUrl`, and neither the cancel handler nor the close handler revokes it. There is also no `useEffect` cleanup. So completed setup runs can leave Blob URLs (containing backup codes) alive for the session, accumulating across repeated setups and keeping sensitive data in memory longer than intended.
